key_headlines.title: South Korea Achieves Historic $1 Trillion Annual Export Milestone
key_headlines.summary: South Korea has surpassed $1 trillion in annual exports for the first time in history, with semiconductors accounting for 43% of total exports. The achievement was driven by strong performance in HBM chips and automobiles, alongside contributions from cosmetics and other sectors.

key_headlines.title: US Approves Export of 880,000 Nvidia and AMD Chips to China Despite Restrictions
key_headlines.summary: The US approved the export of approximately 880,000 AI chips from Nvidia and AMD to Chinese companies including Tencent and Alibaba in the first half of 2026, including advanced H200 chips. This contradicts stated US policies to restrict semiconductor exports to China and entities supporting the People's Liberation Army.

key_headlines.title: South Korea's Trade Deficit with China Widens Excluding Semiconductors by $41.5 Billion
key_headlines.summary: While Korea achieved a trade surplus with China for the first time in 4 years, this masks a $41.5 billion deficit when semiconductors are excluded. Rising Chinese electric vehicle imports and declining Korean auto exports contribute to the concerning trend, highlighting excessive reliance on semiconductor exports.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Crashes Below 4,900 Mark in 'Black Friday' as Market Drops Over 5%
key_headlines.summary: South Korean stock markets experienced a significant selloff on November 20, with both KOSPI and KOSDAQ plummeting over 5% amid global tech stock weakness. Foreign investors and institutions dumped over 2 trillion won, with major semiconductor companies like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix leading the decline.

key_headlines.title: Producer Prices Fall 0.1% in October After 3-Month Climb Amid Agricultural Gains
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's October producer prices declined 0.1% month-on-month for the first time in three months as apple prices fell 29% and pork prices dropped 13% following the Chuseok holiday. Despite improvements in agricultural products, manufactured goods prices continued rising due to international oil price increases.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea has reached an unprecedented $1 trillion in annual exports, with semiconductors and automobiles emerging as key drivers, alongside cosmetics and other sectors. However, deeper analysis reveals concerning structural imbalances, as the country's trade surplus with China excluding semiconductors shows a $41.5 billion deficit, indicating excessive dependence on chip exports. Small and medium enterprises have also achieved record export volumes, surpassing $100 billion for the first time. Experts emphasize the need for sustained policy focus on non-semiconductor industry productivity improvements and wage growth to maintain long-term sustainable economic expansion beyond semiconductor sector achievements.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Bank of Korea's monetary policy committee is set to decide on the benchmark interest rate on November 26, with markets closely monitoring whether a rate hike will occur as the year concludes. The decision comes amid concerns about the KOSPI's collapse below the 4,900 mark and the need to balance inflation concerns against economic growth considerations. US inflation data, particularly the PCE price index, will significantly influence the Fed's December decision-making and subsequently impact Korean financial markets. The domestic government is evaluating implications of potential US tariff increases on Korean exports, particularly in automobiles and auto parts, as Korea's trade surplus with the US exceeds $100 billion for the first time.
sections.Financial Markets: South Korean stock markets experienced a severe selloff on November 20, with KOSPI and KOSDAQ both plummeting over 5% in what was termed a 'Black Friday' market crash. Foreign investors and institutions triggered over 2 trillion won in net sales, with semiconductor giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix leading declines as risk-aversion sentiment dominated. The anticipated positive impact from Anthropic's IPO failed to materialize, with the AI company's stock declining 8.5% on its second trading day, raising broader concerns about AI sector valuations and sustainability. Government bond yields fell sharply as investors fled to safer assets, while the market braces for the Bank of Korea's rate decision and US inflation data as key upcoming catalysts.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's trade relationship with China reveals significant structural vulnerabilities when semiconductors are excluded from analysis, with a $41.5 billion deficit indicating weakness in automobiles, batteries, and electrical equipment sectors. Chinese electric vehicle imports continue rising while Korean automobile exports to China decline, partially due to Korean battery manufacturers relocating production to China to manage higher domestic production costs. High-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips have emerged as a major export success story after 13 years of skepticism, with SK Hynix leading development efforts and contributing substantially to Korea's semiconductor export boom. The automotive sector has also demonstrated impressive growth, with exports increasing 5.4 times over 25 years, though recent market dynamics suggest this growth may be moderating.
sections.Real Estate: South Korea's residential rental market faces critical structural challenges as the shortage of monthly lease and jeonse rental properties has become more severe than price-related issues, with concerns that Seoul's non-homeowning tenants will be displaced to Gyeonggi Province. The upcoming 2027 increase in property holding taxes threatens to further exacerbate the rental shortage as landlords shift tax burdens to tenants or reduce rental supply. Next week's supply surge shows 6,295 units across 15 nationwide locations receiving subscription applications, representing a 3.7-fold increase compared to the previous week, with new offerings in Seoul's Yeongdeungpo and Jongno districts. The government maintained the 2027 official property valuation rate (current realization rate) at 69.0%, unchanged from 2026, though property holding taxes are expected to increase in areas where actual property values have appreciated.
sections.International Economy: Global stock markets experienced significant volatility with the US NASDAQ falling 5.3%, while the Dow Jones and S&P 500 entered correction territory amid technical stock selling and concerns about Nvidia's accounting practices under SEC investigation. Trump administration officials expressed concerns about the Federal Reserve's interest rate policies, with some suggesting that lower rates could have enabled higher GDP growth rates comparable to India's current performance. South Korea faces potential escalation in US tariff pressures, particularly targeting automobiles and auto parts rather than electronic products, as the country's trade surplus with the US surpasses $100 billion for the first time. Fed officials have signaled that all policy options remain on the table for December's FOMC meeting, with some suggesting the possibility of further rate increases to address AI-driven economic overheating concerns.
sections.AI & Economy: Anthropic's highly anticipated IPO, which raised record capital for an AI company, failed to spark market enthusiasm, with the stock declining 8.5% on its second trading day, signaling growing concerns about AI sector valuations and profitability timelines. AI infrastructure investment concerns have intensified, with copper prices declining 16% from recent highs as market participants grow worried about delays in US data center construction and slower-than-expected implementation of AI projects. President Lee visited SK's hyperscale AI data center project in Ulsan, capable of accommodating 60,000 advanced GPUs and expected to generate 25 trillion won in economic impact and 78,000 jobs over 30 years. The AI sector now faces challenges including financing difficulties for companies dependent on Nvidia's financial support, rising concerns about construction costs and timelines, and regulatory scrutiny, particularly regarding AI-enabled cheating in national certification exams.
sections.Others: The government labor ministry conducted inspections of national certification exam sites following recent controversies over AI-enabled cheating, emphasizing the need for stronger examination supervision and integrity measures. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's unexpected departure from the company has triggered widespread speculation about succession and potential strategic shifts, with prominent figures including Elon Musk and President Trump calling for his return. HS Chemical received the highest safety management evaluation rating (SA1) for construction safety, contributing to improved workplace safety standards across Korean industry. Various startups and companies have reported business developments and financial achievements, though broader economic uncertainty continues to impact investment sentiment and business expansion plans.
